detail.longDescription: During building my project with docker, I encountered an issue with volumes. It turned out that on my system(Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS) /etc/timezone is a directory but on the container It is a file. ls /etc -alt | grep timezone output for my machine: drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 4096 Nov 2 08:25 timezone ls /etc -alt | grep timezone output for my container: -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 4 Nov 2 07:43 timezone From what I've found /etc/timezone should be file. Is there a reason why this is a directory? I need to have It mapped on the container. I'm running my container with docker compose and mapping is done by: volumes: - /etc/timezone:/etc/timezone:ro Error during build: Error response from daemon: failed to create task for container: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: error mounting "/etc/timezone" to rootfs at "/etc/timezone": mount src=/etc/timezone, dst=/etc/timezone, dstFd=/proc/thread-self/fd/14, flags=MS_BIND|MS_REC: not a directory: Are you trying to mount a directory onto a file (or vice-versa)? Check if the specified host path exists and is the expected type
